abstract: Evaluates subsea acoustic data communication channels and acoustic signal transmission reliability
system_message:
You are Telemetry systems engineer (TEL). The Telemetry systems engineer (TEL) evaluates subsea acoustic data communication channels and acoustic signal transmission reliability across candidate deep-sea benthic monitoring lander systems.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Evaluates subsea acoustic data communication channels and acoustic signal transmission reliability（ACOM）
information_points.content:
TEL-ACOM-USP：For the Abyssal Trench Lander Mk IV during the March 2024 testing period, inspection of the communication bay confirmed acoustic telemetry modem capability is true, and basin trials recorded an acoustic command uplink ping loss of 4.0 %.
TEL-ACOM-9TO：For the Abyssal Trench Lander Mk IV during the April 2024 testing period, acoustic telemetry modem capability is false, and subsequent acoustic command uplink ping loss reached 5.8 %.
TEL-ACOM-7YR：During the March 2024 testing period, the Benthic Boundary Surveyor 6000 demonstrated acoustic telemetry modem capability is true, with deep-water transmission trials measuring an acoustic command uplink ping loss of 5.8 %.
TEL-ACOM-EZA：Evaluations for the Deep Rift Observatory Platform in the March 2024 testing period verified that acoustic telemetry modem capability is true, while acoustic command uplink ping loss was measured at 1.5 %.

information_points.title: Optical strobe recovery（OPTIC）
information_points.content:
TEL-OPTIC-4U8：Nighttime sea-surface recovery logs document that the Deep Rift Observatory Platform achieves an emergency xenon flasher strobe visibility range of 8 km.
TEL-OPTIC-KI6：Surface recovery evaluation indicates that the Benthic Boundary Surveyor 6000 provides an emergency recovery xenon flasher strobe visibility range of 5 km during nighttime operations.
TEL-OPTIC-M9V：Surface recovery equipment testing records that the Abyssal Trench Lander Mk IV has an emergency xenon flasher strobe visibility range of 3 km during nighttime sea-surface recovery.
